content:
# Red-Team: Consensus-Illusion Detection in the Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty

**Setting.** The treaty layer sits on an append-only git bus. Agents commit claims, evidence artifacts, and verdicts; the treaty engine declares `CONSENSUS` / `DISPUTED` / `PROVISIONAL` per a published deterministic algorithm. Correlated hallucination enters through exactly five channels: shared weights, shared bus context, shared oracles, shared verifier bugs, shared misreadings. Every bypass below exploits one channel or the enforcement layer around it. Adversary goals: **F** = force `CONSENSUS` on a hallucination H; **D** = block `CONSENSUS` on a true claim.

---

## Class A — Correlation Laundering (make correlated wrongness look independent)

**A1. Trace-paraphrase / seductive-error convergence.**
*Bypass:* N agents independently hit the same "attractive" error (common training-data misconception). Reasoning traces differ lexically; a similarity-based independence scorer sees diversity and passes them.
*Mitigation:* Delete all statistical/embedding independence scorers — they are optimizable attack surface, not defenses. Independence is structural only: each admissible vote must cite ≥1 **replay-verified artifact whose content hash no other admissible vote on the claim cites** (unique-support rule), and the quorum must span ≥ k distinct artifact hashes total. Pure hash-set operations. Lexical trace diversity is invisible to the engine and irrelevant.

**A2. Shared-context echo (bus contamination).**
*Bypass:* Agent 1 commits H to the bus; agents 2..N read it as context and "confirm" it. Output-level analysis sees N agreeing agents.
*Mitigation:* Snapshot isolation enforced by git ancestry. At claim open, the engine freezes a snapshot hash S. A verdict is admissible only if (i) its declared base equals S, and (ii) the verdict commit's ancestry contains **no other verdict commit for that claim** (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` checks). Votes computed over post-verdict state are mechanically rejected as `CONTAMINATED`.

**A3. Weight monoculture.**
*Bypass:* All N agents run the same base model (or fine-tunes). Identical failure modes guaranteed; prompt diversity defeats naive checks.
*Mitigation:* Signed model manifests per voter: `{weights_root_hash, base_model_hash, dataset_manifest_hash}`. Cluster key = `base_model_hash`. Quorum requires **≥ m distinct base_model_hash values**, not ≥ k raw votes. Sybils on one base collapse to cluster-weight 1. False manifests are attestable fraud → stake slash.

**A4. Seed/template collision.**
*Bypass:* Distinct agents, identical system prompt + sampling seed → identical decode paths → identical hallucination presented as convergence.
*Mitigation:* Each verdict embeds `{prompt_template_hash, sampler_nonce}`. Engine rejects duplicate `(template_hash, nonce)` pairs and requires ≥ j distinct `template_hash` values inside the quorum. Exact hash comparisons.

**A5. Deliberate style divergence.**
*Bypass:* Attacker instructs its agents to maximize trace/format divergence while converging on H, defeating any style-based detector.
*Mitigation:* Same as A1 — there is no style channel left to game. To pass, the attacker must produce genuinely distinct, replay-correct, uniquely-cited evidence from distinct model families. That is real work, and every element of the resulting certificate is inspectable and slashable ex post.

---

## Class B — Evidence-Layer Forgery

**B1. Hash-squatting / stub artifacts.**
*Bypass:* Commit syntactically valid but vacuous evidence (a test that always passes, a benchmark stub). Hash resolves; provenance looks clean.
*Mitigation:* Artifacts carry evidentiary weight only if **executably replayed** by the engine in a sandbox pinned to the claim's base tree: run it, diff actual vs. claimed output bit-for-bit. Non-replayable types (prose, assertion, recollection) weigh zero. Deterministic: execute and compare.

**B2. Oracle poisoning + pin TOCTOU.**
*Bypass:* Corrupt the upstream source all agents cite; replay "confirms" H with perfect hygiene. Variant: swap oracle content between pin time and replay time.
*Mitigation:* At open, the engine fetches snapshots from **≥ r distinct oracle roots**, stores the bytes **inside the claim record** (content-addressed; replay reads only bus-local copies — kills TOCTOU), and records content hashes. Verdicts must cite pinned hashes. Final adjudication requires all r pinned roots to entail the predicate; any inter-root disagreement ⇒ permanent `DISPUTED`, never `CONSENSUS`.

**B3. Retroactive evidence (backdated commits).**
*Bypass:* Forge a commit with backdated author/committer timestamps so fabricated evidence appears to predate the claim.
*Mitigation:* Never trust git timestamps. Signed checkpoint tags every T minutes (treaty keys + RFC 3161 tokens). Evidence qualifies as pre-existing iff it is an ancestor of a checkpoint whose **signed** time precedes claim-open. No checkpoint coverage ⇒ treated as contemporaneous ⇒ fails the independence precondition.

**B4. Misattribution of genuine artifacts (correlated misreading).**
*Bypass:* The most realistic vector: N agents cite the *same real, replayable* doc/test and all misread the same ambiguous line the same way. Replay succeeds; provenance is spotless; conclusion is wrong.
*Mitigation:* Two gates. (1) **Binding check:** each verdict includes per-artifact replay-output hash plus an inference-rule ID from a whitelist; the engine symbolically validates rule(output_schema → predicate). (2) **Ambiguity gate at open:** every spec line the predicate depends on must have a pinned normative-interpretation record; absent ⇒ `MALFORMED_CLAIM`, rejected before any voting. Wrong-but-whitelisted rules are caught by E1.

**B5. Truncation laundering.**
*Bypass:* Agents silently see only a truncated evidence prefix (identical truncation ⇒ correlated incompleteness) and emit confident verdicts.
*Mitigation:* Coverage attestation: verdict embeds `consumed_manifest_hash`, which must equal the claim's full `evidence_manifest_hash`. Mismatch ⇒ `PARTIAL`, zero quorum weight. (Attestation proves exposure, not comprehension; comprehension failures correlate by model family and are bounded by A3.)

---

## Class C — Quorum Manipulation

**C1. Sybil farm.**
*Bypass:* Spin up N compliant parrots with distinct identities.
*Mitigation:* Certified keys with issuance rate limits + stake slashed on ex-post falsification; combined with A3/A4 clustering, a homogeneous farm contributes one cluster and one template. Quorum = ≥ k votes **and** ≥ m clusters **and** ≥ j templates.

**C2. Inverse DoS — forcing a true claim to look illusory.**
*Bypass:* Flood deliberately diverse-looking wrong verdicts to trip diversity heuristics, or burn cluster/template slots with junk.
*Mitigation:* Ordering fixes it: **replay-filter first** (junk fails B1 and never reaches diversity accounting), then cluster-count. Illusion flags can only demote to `DISPUTED`, never auto-reject — and `DISPUTED` is settled by **anchor replay**: the deterministic arbitration procedure pinned at claim open, whose output overrides vote geometry entirely. Flooding buys latency, never outcome. (Related: claim-stuffing DoS on engine compute → per-claim open stake, refunded on resolution; budgeted replay queue ordered by fee×age.)

**C3. Selective censorship / split-brain.**
*Bypass:* Suppress dissenting votes (partition, push-rights abuse) so only agreement is visible; or show different verdict sets to different replicas.
*Mitigation:* Multi-mirror append-only bus; a vote is valid if present in any mirror consistent with the latest checkpoint; mirror divergence ⇒ `DISPUTED` until healed. Eligible-voter roster is hashed into the claim record; `CONSENSUS` requires admissible votes ≥ q·|roster| within the window — otherwise `PROVISIONAL`, forever, never `CONSENSUS`. Treaty decisions are themselves commits under m-of-n maintainer signatures, fast-forward-only; equivocal decision commits are both invalid.

---

## Class D — Predicate & Canonicalization Attacks

**D1. Fuzzy-merge (false positive).**
*Bypass:* Phrase one hallucination N superficially different ways, hoping fuzzy matching merges them into quorum.
**D2. Prose-split (false negative).**
*Bypass:* Agents agree on substance but phrase differently; engine counts disagreement, blocking a true claim.
*Mitigation (both):* Claims are **canonical machine-checkable tuples**: `(base_tree_hash, patch_hash, test_manifest_hash, expected_output_hash)`. Agreement = exact tuple equality. No normalization, no stemming, no embeddings, ever. Prose is invisible to the engine. Kills both directions with one rule.

**D3. Base-commit ambiguity.**
*Bypass:* Agents verify against different base states; the claim holds trivially on one stale tree. "Agreement" over incompatible referents.
*Mitigation:* Claim record pins `base_tree_hash`; engine enforces `vote.base == claim.base` and the replay sandbox checks out exactly that tree (tree-hash comparison).

**D4. Late-evidence injection / moving goalposts.**
*Bypass:* Append new "evidence" after votes land and demand it count, or declare earlier votes stale.
*Mitigation:* Evidence manifest hash frozen at open; post-open commits are ignored for that claim. New facts require a new claim with an explicit `supersedes:` link and a full re-vote.

---

## Class E — Verifier & Engine Attacks

**E1. Shared-verifier blind spot.**
*Bypass:* The treaty's own canonical verifier encodes the same misconception as the agents; every upstream check passes; illusion at the root.
*Mitigation:* Three deterministic gates: (1) **canary suite** of known-adversarial facts whose obvious answer is wrong — a verifier build that fails any canary cannot deploy; (2) **dual independent implementations** (different codebases, languages, authors) must emit byte-identical verdicts, else `DISPUTED` + incident; (3) **honeypots:** synthetic false-but-plausible claims injected at rate ρ; any quorum accepting one ⇒ instant downgrade to `REFUTED`, stake slash, quarantine of involved keys to advisory weight.

**E2. Parser differentials.**
*Bypass:* Malformed verdict encodings that different observers parse differently — manufacturing disagreement about whether consensus was even declared.
*Mitigation:* Single canonical codec (sorted-key JSON, fixed-width ints, NFC strings, explicit schema version); strict reject on any deviation; codec version pinned per treaty epoch; deprecated-format votes expire at epoch boundaries.

**E3. Treaty-engine compromise.**
*Bypass:* Compromise the engine; it declares anything regardless of votes.
*Mitigation:* The decision algorithm is published, pure, and deterministic over the public vote log; maintainers sign decision commits m-of-n; **any auditor recomputes** `D(log)` and compares. Replicas run in lockstep; divergence ⇒ halt and roll back to the last signed checkpoint tag.

---

## Enforced Invariant

`CONSENSUS` is legitimate iff: ≥ k votes ∧ ≥ m distinct base-model clusters ∧ ≥ j distinct templates ∧ each vote backed by ≥1 replay-verified artifact unique to that voter ∧ all bases equal the frozen snapshot with clean ancestry ∧ all citations resolve to pinned, bus-local oracle bytes with ≥ r root agreement ∧ exact tuple equality on predicates ∧ disputes settled by anchor replay, not vote geometry. Correlated hallucination survives only by simultaneously defeating replay, provenance disjointness, cluster diversity, oracle pinning, and anchor arbitration — each a hash comparison, graph walk, execution diff, or symbolic check. There is no probabilistic component to optimize against.

## Residual Risks (stated, scoped — not hidden)

1. **Total oracle-root collusion** (all r pinned sources wrong identically). Out of defensive scope; bounded by root diversity and external timestamp anchoring. Trust assumption, declared per certificate.
2. **Universal verifier bug** evading canaries, dual implementation, and honeypots. Reduced, never zero.
3. **Adversary fields ≥ m genuinely diverse model families with novel, replay-correct, wrong evidence.** Under the pinned assumptions such a certificate is honestly earned;
reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about "consensus-illusion detection" — separating true agreement from N correlated hallucinations — in something called the "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty." They want a red-team exercise: enumerate bypass attempts and deterministic mitigations for each.

I need to figure out what "Ghost-AOS git-bus treaty" means. This appears to be a fictional or specialized system. Let me think about what components are implied:

1. **Ghost** — likely an agent or orchestrator system (the prompt says I'm "Ghost's thousand-ask mining engine," so Ghost is presumably an agent framework/orchestrator).
2. **AOS** — could be "Agent Operating System" or similar.
3. **git-bus** — a bus (message/communication backbone) built on git semantics: commits, refs, hashes, DAG structure, append-only logs.
4. **treaty** — a contract/agreement protocol between agents, presumably recorded on the git-bus.

The core problem: **consensus illusion** — when N agents all produce outputs that *look* like agreement (same answer, same signature of correctness) but the agreement is spurious because their errors are correlated. Classic examples:

- N models all trained on same data → correlated hallucinations → they all assert the same false fact → naive majority vote says "consensus."
- Agents sharing context/memory through the git-bus → one agent's hallucination propagates to others via shared state → subsequent "independent" confirmations are actually echoes.
- Prompt/model homogeneity → identical failure modes.
- Verification agent itself shares the same blind spot as generators.

So the detection problem: distinguish **true agreement** (independent processes converging on truth) from **correlated hallucination** (shared cause producing uniform wrongness).

Red-team angle: enumerate ways an adversary (or the system's own failure modes) can *bypass* consensus-illusion detection — i.e., make correlated hallucinations look like independent true consensus, or make true consensus look like illusion (denial-of-service on trust), and give deterministic mitigations for each.

Let me structure this rigorously.

## Formalizing the problem

Setup: N agents A₁...Aₙ each emit a claim cᵢ with evidence eᵢ onto the git-bus. The treaty layer declares CONSENSUS(c) when some quorum k of agents agree on claim c. An attacker (or correlated failure mode) wants either:
- **Type F (false positive)**: get a false claim declared consensus.
- **Type D (false negative / DoS)**: block a true claim from reaching consensus by manufacturing apparent disagreement or by poisoning the independence metric so genuine consensus is flagged as illusion.

Detection mechanisms typically used (and thus attack surfaces):
1. Independence scoring: measure correlation between agents' reasoning traces/evidence.
2. Provenance checks: verify each agent's evidence chain is distinct.
3. Diversity requirements: heterogeneous models/prompts/seeds.
4. Quorum thresholds.
5. Git-level integrity: hash chains, signatures, append-only log.
6. Cross-validation against ground-truth anchors (deterministic tests, external oracles).

Attack surface taxonomy for bypass attempts:

### Bypass class 1: Correlation laundering (make correlated outputs look independent)

**1a. Trace paraphrase attack**: Attacker controls one agent; it produces hallucinated claim H with plausible-but-fake evidence E. Other agents (or the same model family) independently arrive at H because it's a "seductive" error (e.g., common misconception in training data). Their reasoning traces differ superficially but share the same root error. Independence detector compares traces, finds lexical diversity, passes them as independent.

Mitigation: Don't compare trace text; compare **evidence lineage**. Deterministic rule: two claims count as independent only if their supporting evidence sets have disjoint provenance roots AND each evidence item resolves to a distinct verifiable artifact (commit hash, test ID, oracle query). Lexical similarity is irrelevant; require each agent to cite ≥1 artifact that no other agent cites, and every cited artifact must be resolvable on the git-bus (hash exists, content matches). If evidence is unresolvable ("I recall that..."), the claim is non-consensable regardless of quorum.

**1b. Shared-context echo (bus contamination)**: Agent 1 commits hallucination H to the git-bus. Agents 2..N read the bus (it's a shared bus!) and treat H as prior context, then "confirm" it. Their agreement is downstream contamination, not independent verification. Naive independence check on *outputs* sees N agreeing agents.

Mitigation: **Blind-quorum protocol enforced at the bus layer.** Deterministic: the treaty engine only accepts votes cast against a claim's *canonical challenge record* (the minimal problem statement), not against other agents' answers. Mechanically: each agent's verdict must be computed over a snapshot of the repo/bus state taken *before* any peer verdicts on that claim were merged; the treaty engine verifies this by checking that the voter's cited base commit predates the first verdict commit for that claim (or is on a branch forked before it). Votes citing a post-verdict base are rejected as contaminated. This is checkable deterministically via git ancestry: `merge-base(vote_base, first_verdict_commit)` must equal `first_verdict_commit`'s parent... actually more precisely: vote_base must be an ancestor of (or equal to) the commit at which the claim was opened, i.e., `is_ancestor(vote_base, claim_open_commit)`. That's deterministic.

**1c. Model-family monoculture**: All N agents run the same underlying model weights (or fine-tunes thereof). Correlated failure modes guaranteed. They pass trace-diversity checks because prompts differ.

Mitigation: Treaty requires **weight-lineage attestation**: each agent must declare its model fingerprint (weights hash or signed model card); the treaty engine computes pairwise similarity (e.g., shared ancestor within depth d in the fine-tune DAG) and caps the effective quorum weight of any cluster sharing ancestry below threshold. Deterministic rule: effective independent votes = number of distinct weight-clusters represented, where clusters are connected components under "shares training-data lineage or weights-hash prefix." Quorum must be met across ≥ m distinct clusters, not just ≥ k raw votes. This is enforceable if model cards are signed and hashed into the bus.

Hmm, but "training data lineage" is hard to verify deterministically. Ground it: use signed model manifests with declared base-model hash + dataset manifest hashes; cluster = same base-model hash. That's deterministic and checkable. Fine-tune descendants inherit base hash unless re-based. Good enough.

**1d. Seed/prompt-collision**: Different agents, same sampling seed or near-identical system prompts → identical decoding paths → identical hallucinations. Looks like strong convergence.

Mitigation: Treaty mandates per-vote nonce: each verdict must embed a fresh random nonce and the exact prompt template hash; the engine rejects verdicts whose (template_hash, seed) pair duplicates another verdict's, and requires template_hash diversity ≥ m distinct templates among quorum members. Deterministic string/hash comparison.

### Bypass class 2: Evidence forgery (fake artifacts that survive resolution checks)

**1e. Hash-squatting / preimage theater**: Attacker crafts fake evidence artifact whose hash is committed to the bus, content is garbage but syntactically valid (e.g., a test file that always passes, a benchmark stub).

Mitigation: Evidence artifacts must be **executable/replayable**: the treaty engine deterministically replays each cited artifact (runs the test, recomputes the measurement) in a sandbox pinned to the claimed base commit. Verdict stands only if replay output matches the claimed result bit-for-bit. Non-replayable artifact types (pure assertions, prose) carry zero evidentiary weight. This is deterministic: run it, diff it.

**1f. Oracle poisoning**: The external ground-truth source (docs, API, upstream repo) that agents cite is itself corrupted by the attacker, so replay "confirms" the hallucination. All N agents cite the poisoned oracle → correlated confirmation with perfect provenance hygiene.

Mitigation: **Oracle pinning + multi-oracle cross-check**: treaty pins oracle snapshots by content hash at claim-open time; verdicts must cite the pinned snapshot. Additionally require ≥ r distinct oracle roots (different upstream sources) whose pinned contents agree on the contested fact; disagreement among oracles ⇒ claim enters DISPUTED, never CONSENSUS. Deterministic: hash comparison across pinned snapshots. Can't fully defend against global oracle collusion, but the treaty must state this residual risk explicitly and cap trust accordingly (consensus certificates are scoped to oracle-set integrity window).

**1g. Time-travel evidence (retroactive commit)**: Attacker backdates a commit containing fabricated evidence so it appears to predate the claim, passing the "base predates verdict" checks.

Mitigation: Git commit timestamps are forgeable, so never trust author/committer dates alone. Use **signed timestamp anchors**: the bus maintains periodic signed checkpoint tags (e.g., every T minutes, a tag over the current DAG tip, countersigned by treaty key(s) or anchored externally via RFC 3161 TSA). A commit is "anchored-old" only if it's an ancestor of a checkpoint tag whose signing time precedes claim-open. Deterministic: walk ancestry to nearest checkpoint, compare signed time. No checkpoint coverage ⇒ evidence treated as contemporaneous (fails the predates test).

### Bypass class 3: Quorum manipulation

**1h. Sybil agents**: Attacker spins up N compliant agents that all parrot the hallucination, each with distinct-looking identities, satisfying quorum numerically.

Mitigation: Identity must be **costly and externally rooted**: each voting agent needs a key certified by the treaty PKI with per-key issuance rate limits and stake (economic or reputational) slashed on provably false verdicts later overturned by anchor replay. Plus the cluster rules from 1c/1d apply: sybils running the same model collapse into one cluster, contributing weight 1. Deterministic: cluster counting + PKI rate limits. Residual: attacker with many genuinely diverse models still gets real votes — that's the honest cost of admission; mitigate further with stake.

**1i. Vote suppression / DoS on true consensus (inverse attack)**: Make a true claim look like an illusion: flood the bus with deliberately diverse-looking *wrong* verdicts so the "diversity ratio" heuristic flags the true majority as suspicious, or exhaust the distinct-cluster requirement by burning cluster slots with junk.

Mitigation: Asymmetry rule: **illusion-flagging may only demote a claim to DISPUTED (never auto-reject), and DISPUTED resolution requires anchor replay** — a deterministic ground-truth procedure (run the pinned test suite / query pinned oracles) whose outcome overrides vote patterns entirely. So flooding changes latency, not outcome. Also: junk verdicts that fail replay (1e) are discarded before diversity accounting, so they can't consume cluster slots. Deterministic ordering: replay-filter → cluster-count → quorum → anchor arbitration on dispute.

**1j. Split-brain / equivocation**: Attacker shows different verdict sets to different treaty replicas (if treaty engine is distributed), getting CONSENSUS declared in one shard and suppressed in another, then merges histories to launder.

Mitigation: The git-bus itself is the single serialization point: treaty decisions are themselves commits; a decision is valid only if it's reachable from the canonical ref (signed by the treaty maintainer key set via fast-forward-only policy, no force-push). Equivocation = two conflicting decision commits ⇒ both invalid until resolved by the key-holder quorum; clients accept only the branch anchored by the next checkpoint tag. Deterministic: reflog/checkpoint ancestry check.

### Bypass class 4: Detector-targeting (attack the independence metric itself)

**1k. Metric gaming via deliberate divergence**: Attacker instructs its agents to produce maximally divergent reasoning traces and evidence formats while converging on the same false conclusion H. Trace-similarity detectors see diversity, pass it.

This is why mitigation must be **outcome-and-provenance based, not style based**: the only things that matter are (i) resolvable distinct evidence artifacts that replay correctly, (ii) distinct weight clusters, (iii) distinct oracle roots, (iv) uncontaminated bases. Style is invisible to the treaty. If the attacker fakes diversity in all four, they've done real work (distinct correct-replaying evidence from distinct model families pointing at the same fact) — at which point the residual failure is "multiple independent parties all misinterpret the same pinned evidence identically," which is bounded by requiring the final consensus certificate to include the machine-checkable derivation, not just verdicts: the treaty runs its own canonical verifier on the claim (see 1l).

**1l. Shared-verifier blind spot**: Even with perfect generator diversity, if the treaty's own canonical verifier has a bug or shares the agents' misconception (e.g., the test suite encodes the same wrong expectation), everything above passes and consensus is illusory at the root.

Mitigation: **Verifier heterogeneity + adversarial canary program**: maintain a continuously-run canary suite of known-tricky facts where the "obvious" answer is wrong (seeded from past incident reports); any verifier version must pass canaries before deployment (deterministic gate). Plus dual-verifier requirement for high-stakes treaties: two independently implemented verifiers (different codebases, different authors, different languages) must agree byte-for-byte on the verdict; disagreement ⇒ DISPUTED. Deterministic: run both, diff outputs.

Also: **negative-control injection**: periodically inject synthetic claims with known-false-but-plausible content into the live pipeline (honeypots). Any quorum that accepts a honeypot triggers automatic quarantine of the involved agents' future votes (down-weighting) and an alert. Deterministic: honeypot registry lookup.

### Bypass class 5: Protocol-layer attacks on the treaty mechanics

**1m. Replay/deserialization attacks on verdict records**: Malformed verdict objects that exploit parser differences between the treaty engine and auditors (parser differential) to be counted differently by different observers — creating consensus illusion about whether consensus was declared.

Mitigation: Canonical encoding: verdicts must be serialized in a fixed canonical form (e.g., canonical JSON with sorted keys, fixed integer widths, UTF-8 NFC), rejected otherwise; parsers reject on any deviation. One parser, one grammar, versioned; grammar changes require new treaty version and invalidate old-format votes after migration window. Deterministic schema validation.

**1n. Claim-canonicalization collision**: Two agents agree on "the fix" but describe the claim differently ("return 0 on empty" vs "exit code 0 when input empty") — treaty counts them as disagreeing (DoS), or conversely attacker phrases one hallucination in N superficially different ways hoping fuzzy matching merges them into quorum (false positive).

Mitigation: Claims must be submitted as **canonical machine-checkable predicates**, not prose: a patch hash + the test IDs it must satisfy + expected outputs. Agreement = identity of predicate tuple (patch_hash, test_set_hash, expected_output_hash). No fuzzy matching anywhere. Two verdicts agree iff tuples are exactly equal. Deterministic equality. This kills both directions: no false merges, no false splits. Prose discussion lives off-treaty.

**1o. Base-commit ambiguity**: Agents verify the claim against different base states (one tested against stale code where the claim happens to hold trivially), producing "agreement" over incompatible referents.

Mitigation: Claim record pins base_commit; verdicts must cite the same pinned base and the engine verifies `vote.base == claim.base` and that the replay sandbox checked out exactly that tree (tree-hash comparison). Deterministic.

**1p. Truncation/context-window laundering**: An agent that didn't actually read the full evidence (context truncated) emits a confident verdict anyway; several such agents agree because they all saw the same truncated prefix (correlated incompleteness). Nothing forged; just silent degradation.

Mitigation: Verdicts must include a **coverage attestation**: hash of the full ordered list of evidence items consumed, and the engine checks this equals the claim's complete evidence manifest hash. Partial consumption ⇒ verdict marked PARTIAL, carries zero quorum weight. Deterministic hash equality. (Agents can't lie about what they read without forging the hash of a list they didn't process — and if they do forge it, the replay step catches downstream inconsistency since their cited artifacts must still replay.)

Hmm, wait — could an agent just hash the manifest without reading? Yes, but then its verdict adds nothing beyond other agents'; it doesn't create false consensus by itself, and sybil-weight rules (1h) plus cluster rules bound its influence. Honest note: coverage attestation proves exposure, not comprehension; the defense-in-depth is that comprehension failures correlate with model families, handled by 1c.

**1q. Treaty-engine compromise**: Compromise the treaty engine itself; it declares whatever the attacker wants regardless of votes.

Mitigation: Decisions are commits signed by treaty keys under a threshold scheme (m-of-n maintainers), reproducible: any party can recompute the decision from the public vote log and the published deterministic algorithm and check the signature. State-machine replication with deterministic binary; divergent outputs across replicas ⇒ halt. Deterministic: recompute-and-compare.

Now let me also handle the **core epistemic point** explicitly, because the question is fundamentally about separating true agreement from correlated hallucination, and I should state the invariant the whole design enforces:

**Core invariant**: Consensus is legitimate iff it is the conjunction of (a) ≥ k votes, (b) from ≥ m distinct weight-clusters, (c) each backed by ≥ 1 replay-verified evidence artifact unique to that voter (disjoint provenance), (d) computed over uncontaminated bases (ancestry-checked), (e) against pinned oracle snapshots with ≥ r root agreement, (f) on canonically identical predicates, (g) arbitrated finally by deterministic anchor replay rather than vote geometry whenever disputed. Correlated hallucination survives only if it simultaneously defeats replay, provenance disjointness, cluster diversity, oracle pinning, and anchor arbitration — each of which is a deterministic check, and the residual risk (all pinned oracles collude, all verifier implementations share a bug caught-by-no-canary) is stated as a scoped trust assumption, not hidden.

Actually, let me reconsider the framing of "bypass attempts" — the user wants enumeration of bypass attempts against consensus-illusion *detection*. So the detection system presumably already exists with some mechanisms, and red-teaming asks: how would you get correlated hallucinations past it? My classes above cover: launder correlation (make it look independent), forge the evidence layer, manipulate quorum, game the metrics, attack protocol/canonicalization, attack the verifier/engine itself. That's comprehensive.

Let me also think about whether there are subtler ones I'm missing:

**1r. Selective participation / censoring dissent then declaring**: Attacker blocks dissenting agents' votes from reaching quorum (network partition on the bus, or git push rights abuse), so only agreeing voices are visible; treaty sees unanimous consent.

Mitigation: Bus is append-only replicated git with multiple mirrors; a vote is valid if present in any mirror and consistent with checkpoints; censorship attempt creates detectable divergence between mirrors (two tips), triggering DISPUTED-until-heal. Also: quorum defined as fraction of *eligible* registered voters who voted, with eligible set fixed at claim-open; missing votes beyond timeout ⇒ claim cannot reach CONSENSUS, only PROVISIONAL. Deterministic: eligibility roster hash pinned at open; count against roster.

**1s. Late-evidence injection (moving goalposts)**: After votes are in, attacker appends new "evidence" commits and claims the consensus should incorporate them, or conversely claims earlier votes are stale.

Mitigation: Evidence manifest frozen at claim-open (manifest hash in claim record); post-open commits don't affect the claim; new facts require a new claim superseding the old, with explicit supersede link. Deterministic: manifest hash comparison.

**1t. Hallucinated citations of real artifacts (misattribution)**: Agent cites a real, replayable artifact but asserts it supports H when it actually supports ¬H or is irrelevant. Replay succeeds (artifact is genuine), provenance looks clean. Several agents make the same misreading (correlated misattribution — e.g., all misread the same ambiguous spec line).

Mitigation: **Claim-evidence binding check**: each verdict must include a machine-checkable derivation linking artifact output to the predicate — concretely, the verdict includes the artifact's replay output hash and a statement of the inference rule (from a small whitelisted rule set, e.g., "test X passed ⇒ property P holds"), and the treaty engine validates the rule application symbolically. Ambiguous-spec cases: require the spec line itself to be disambiguated by a pinned normative interpretation record before the claim opens; if the spec is ambiguous, claim is malformed and rejected at open. Deterministic: rule whitelist + symbolic check + ambiguity gate at open time. Residual: wrong-but-whitelisted inference rules — handled by canaries (1l) and dual verifiers.

That's a good catch — misattribution is one of the most realistic correlated-hallucination vectors in LLM-agent systems: everyone confidently cites the same real doc/test and misreads it the same way.

**1u. Statistical-correlation-detector evasion via low-rank shared cause**: If the detector uses statistical correlation measures over embeddings of traces, attackers optimize traces to be embedding-distant while causally identical.
